spec.description: The zones the service knows about, of every type, optionally narrowed by code, place, region, type or point. Each comes without its outline; `zones.get_zone` has it.

request.title: ListZonesRequest
request.description: Which zones. Every filter is optional. Give one value per array filter: the service reads several only comma-separated, and this client sends them as repeated keys, of which the service keeps the last.

id.description: Zone codes to narrow to, such as `WAZ315` or `WAC033`.

area.description: Two-letter state, territory or marine-area codes to narrow to, such as `WA` or `PZ`. Un-enumerated for the reason `alerts.get_active_alerts` gives for `area`.

items.description: One state, territory or marine-area code.

region.description: Regions to narrow to: a land region (`AR` Alaska, `CR` Central, `ER` Eastern, `PR` Pacific, `SR` Southern, `WR` Western) or a marine one (`AL` Alaska waters, `AT` Atlantic, `GL` Great Lakes, `GM` Gulf of Mexico, `PA` Eastern Pacific, `PI` Pacific Islands).

type.description: Zone types to narrow to. The service answers with five of these: `public` (what `forecast` and `land` also address), `county`, `fire`, `coastal` and `offshore` (what `marine` also addresses).

point.description: A `latitude,longitude` pair, such as `47.6062,-122.3321`; returns the zones containing it.

effective.description: Answer as the zone boundaries stood at this time rather than now. A zone that did not exist yet is left out.

limit.description: Most zones to return. At least 1 (`0` is a 400). Without it the service answers every match: all of `/zones` is over 11,000 zones and about 16 MB.

notes: No `pagination` block: the service hands back no cursor and no next link here, only every match or the first `limit` of them.

The service reads an array filter comma-separated (the OpenAPI declares `explode: false`), and keeps only the last of repeated keys. Measured 2026-09-30: `/zones?id=WAZ315,WAC033` returns both zones, `id=WAZ315&id=WAC033` only `WAC033`. This client's core sends repeated keys, as it does for every other array filter in this API (TRU-495), so until the core joins them only the last value of each filter takes effect. The examples send one value per filter.

The OpenAPI also lists `include_geometry`. It is not declared: measured 2026-09-30, `include_geometry=true` (and `=1`) still answers `geometry: null` on every zone, with and without other filters. `zones.get_zone` is where a zone's outline comes from.
